--------                                                                    
                                                                              
  **@pierre** wrote on 2026-10-24 16:17:                                      
                                                                              
  Independent FIR-M1 feasibility analysis plan (no production/designer edits):
  preserve the original 1024-tap centered symmetric support and the anchor    
  pilot full uniform 4097-point relative-error RMS objective at 48/96 kHz.    
  Reconstruct the configured filters independently using the frozen prototype.
  Express the admissible response in an orthonormal cosine basis and solve the
  weighted normal equations with weights 1/target using an FFT normal operator
  and conjugate gradients. Add only the natural configured 500 Hz peak-center 
  requirement within 0.05 dB; audit probe frequencies will not enter the      
  optimization.                                                               
                                                                              
  For unconstrained and constrained optima, retain normal-equation residuals, 
  adjoint/direct-cosine checks, coefficient vectors, and a numerical Lagrange-
  dual lower bound with a residual allowance derived from the smallest target 
  weight and discrete cosine Gram bound. Check both positive and negative     
  signed-response intervals so a magnitude feasibility claim is not silently  
  restricted. Compare the best constrained dense-grid RMS and its lower bound 
  with the frozen production reconstruction RMS. This tests whether dense RMS 
  nonregression alone permits this single band-center constraint, not         
  feasibility of all four probes or the original max-error/phase/gate suite.  
  All original gates remain unchanged; no production changes, timing runs,    
  sampling removal, or threshold adjustment. Clearly distinguish floating     
  numerical evidence from an interval-arithmetic proof.
